# Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable, read at start, usually from a `.env`
file beside the binary (`cp .env.example .env`). The older `DIARY_<NAME>`
spelling of each is still accepted. A value that is set but cannot be read stops
the start with the reason rather than falling back to the default.

## Basics

| setting | example | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_USER` | `narl` | The one and only account. Both are checked in constant time on login. |
| `WORKSPACE_PASSWORD` | `change-me` | See the row above. |
| `WORKSPACE_SECRET` | `replace-with-32-random-characters` | Signs session cookies. Rotate it to log every device out. 32+ random chars. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32 |
| `WORKSPACE_DATA_DIR` | `./data` | Where the SQLite database and uploaded media live. |
| `WORKSPACE_BIND` | `127.0.0.1:4242` | Address to listen on. Put a TLS terminating reverse proxy in front of this. |
| `WORKSPACE_SESSION_DAYS` | `30` | How long a login lasts, in days. |
| `WORKSPACE_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` | `1024` | Largest upload, in megabytes: one request, or what an imported zip unpacks to. Uploads stream to disk, so this bounds the disk, not the memory. |
| `WORKSPACE_SECURE_COOKIE` | `0` | Set to 1 once the app is served over HTTPS: the cookie gets `Secure` and the `__Host-` prefix (everyone is logged out once), and browsers are told to use HTTPS only (HSTS). The server refuses to start with the example secret or password above still in place. |

## SFTP mount

| setting | example | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_SFTP_BIND` | `127.0.0.1:2222` | Off until this is set. Once it's up, register a key with `:sshkey add <name> <ssh-ed25519 ...>` in the app, then `sshfs -P <port> anything@host:/ mnt/` (the username is ignored — only the key decides who gets in). On the mount, `mkdir` at the root makes a space and anywhere else a folder; a new `.md` file is a new document. A leading `# Heading` is the document's title. Editor temp, swap and backup files are kept in memory for the session only, and renaming one onto a `.md` name saves it into that document. Under Docker, bind 0.0.0.0 (not 127.0.0.1) as the app listens inside the container — the host-side address in compose.yml's `ports:` is what actually restricts who can reach it. |

## Proton Drive backup

Off until `:backup login <username>` in the workspace (or `narl-workspace proton-login`) stores a session under WORKSPACE_DATA_DIR. These only shape how often the mirror runs.

| setting | example | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_PROTON_DEVICE` | `narl-workspace` | The device the server registers in Proton Drive; its sync root is the folder the diary is mirrored into. |
| `WORKSPACE_BACKUP_INTERVAL_MIN` | `60` | Backstop between runs, in minutes. 0 leaves it change-driven only. |
| `WORKSPACE_BACKUP_DEBOUNCE_SEC` | `300` | How long the diary must be quiet after a change before it is mirrored, so a writing session uploads once rather than after every save. |
| `WORKSPACE_BACKUP_PRUNE` | `0` | Set to 1 to let a deletion here trash the mirrored file there. Off by default: a backup that forgets on command is one accident from being none. |
| `WORKSPACE_SESSION_KEY_FILE` | `/run/secrets/session_key` | Seal the stored Proton session under a key kept off the data volume, so a copy of the volume alone carries no usable session. Point it at a Docker secret (see compose.override.yml.example); `openssl rand -base64 32` makes the key. Losing the key costs a new `proton-login`, nothing more. Unset by default. |

## Notification mail

Off until WORKSPACE_SMTP_URL is set. Nothing is even queued while it is unset.

| setting | example | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_SMTP_URL` | `smtps://mail.example.org:465` | The relay. `smtps://host:465` is implicit TLS, `smtp://host:587?tls=required` is STARTTLS, and a bare `smtp://host:1025` is plain — which only belongs on a local mail catcher. Credentials may live in the URL or in the two variables below. Unset by default. |
| `WORKSPACE_SMTP_USER` |  | See the row above. Unset by default. |
| `WORKSPACE_SMTP_PASSWORD` |  | See the row above. Unset by default. |
| `WORKSPACE_MAIL_FROM` | `workspace@example.org` | Where the mail comes from and goes to. FROM defaults to TO. Unset by default. |
| `WORKSPACE_MAIL_TO` | `you@example.org` | See the row above. Unset by default. |
| `WORKSPACE_TIMEZONE` | `Europe/Berlin` | "Did I write today?" and "is this due today?" are local-day questions, and the answer changes with the timezone rather than with a fixed offset. |
| `WORKSPACE_REMINDER_AT` | `20:00` | When to ask about the diary, if nothing was written in it that day. `off` turns it into no reminder at all. |
| `WORKSPACE_CARD_DUE_AT` | `08:00` | When to mail about cards that are due today or already overdue. |
| `WORKSPACE_DIGEST_AT` | `sun 18:00` | Weekday and time of the weekly digest. |
| `WORKSPACE_MAIL_KINDS` | `reminder,card_due,digest,login` | Which of the four kinds may be sent. Drop one from the list to switch it off. |

## Vault, trash and history

| setting | example | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_VAULT_IDLE_MIN` | `15` | Minutes the vault stays open with nothing using it, before it locks itself. It also locks on logout and whenever the server restarts. |
| `WORKSPACE_TRASH_DAYS` | `30` | Days a deleted document, folder, file or space waits in the trash, where :trash can bring it back, before it and its files are deleted for good. |
| `WORKSPACE_REVISION_DAYS` | `90` | Days a document's earlier versions are kept for :history. The newest 20 of every document are kept however old they are. |
